picks.title: Little Red Dots: One Photometric Tag Concealing Diverse Spectroscopic Flavors of Massive Star Formation and Black Hole Activity
picks.abstract: We compile JWST/NIRSpec prism and MIRI data for 249 Little Red Dots (LRDs) at 2.3 < z < 9.3, forming a representative spectroscopic subset of NIRCam-selected LRDs. We derive a median stacked spectrum covering rest-frame 0.09–1.2 μ m, with MIRI photometry extending the spectral energy distribution to 4 μ m. 49 49 Downloadable from Zenodo: doi: 10.5281/zenodo.22206191. Four additional stacks for subsamples defined by optical-to-UV luminosity ratios show that LRDs form a heterogeneous population spanning diverse continuum slopes and line properties. Assuming LRDs host supermassive black holes (BHs) surrounded by dense gas clouds, and stars accompany this core, we infer masses of M BH ∼ 10 6.0−6.5 M ⊙ and M ⋆ ∼ 10 8.3 M ⊙, corresponding to BH-to-stellar mass ratios of 1%–2%. The stacks show ubiquitous UV and optical Fe II emission, indicating a direct view of the broad-line region and high (but sub-Eddington) accretion (λ Edd = 0.6 ± 0.2). We find a significant stellar contribution in the far-UV, reaching ∼80% in the bluest systems. Possible Wolf–Rayet features (He II λ 4687, nitrogen lines) are identified, tracing a young (3–7 Myr) compact starburst event. We also detect strong Balmer breaks and atypical Balmer, Paschen, [O III], and optical and near-infrared He I line ratios, and an absorption at ∼4550 Å (probably linked to Fe II), all consistent with radiative-transfer effects in high-density gas with warm temperatures (4000–7000 K). We find a diversity of LRD flavors modulated by the luminosity ratio between a short (≲20 Myr) and intense phase of BH activity, the most extreme stage lasting ∼3–7 Myr, characterized by near-Eddington-limit radiation, and a nuclear and compact starburst dominated by massive stars (even supermassive, M SMS ∼ 10 5 M ⊙), all embedded in…

picks.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
picks.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease 1 , 2 . Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling 3 , we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

picks.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
picks.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

picks.title: Cycle affinity and winding localize eigenvalues of Markov generators
picks.abstract: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. We show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector "winding number" of some nonequilibrium cycle. In discrete and continuous unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number is determined by the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In discrete multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl–Seifert ellipse conjecture.

picks.title: Nondichroic enantio-sensitive chiroptical spectroscopy in isotropic media
picks.abstract: Chiroptical effects using circularly polarized light in isotropic media produce signals that change sign when switching either molecular handedness (enantio-sensitivity) or the light helicity (circular dichroism). Here, we break this enantio-sensitive-and-dichroic paradigm by measuring a new type of chiroptical signal which is enantio-sensitive but not dichroic. We photoionize chiral molecules using femtosecond laser pulses and detect the three-dimensional photoelectron momentum distribution. The non-dichroic, enantio-sensitive asymmetry is encoded in octupolar and higher multipolar terms in the photoelectron angular distribution, which appear in multiphoton or strong-field ionization with elliptically polarized fields or cross polarized two-color fields. The robustness of the enantio-sensitivity with respect to the relative phase between the vectorial components of the ionizing field represents an example of symmetry protection, and opens unexplored opportunities for imaging ultrafast dynamics in chiral molecules, such as enantio-sensitive photoelectron spectroscopy with bright squeezed vacuum states.

picks.title: SQuIGG L → E: Ubiquitous Cool Gas Outflows with Large Mass-loading Factors in z ∼ 0.7 Post-starburst Galaxies
picks.abstract: While recent James Webb Space Telescope studies have highlighted cool gas outflows as an important mechanism for rapid quenching at z ≳ 2, such space-based spectroscopic samples remain limited in size. In this work, we search for and characterize cool gas outflows traced by Fe ii λλ 2586, 2600 and Mg ii λλ 2796, 2803 absorption in post-starburst galaxies (PSBs) at 0.5 < z < 0.9, which are accessible to ground-based spectroscopy. Utilizing the SQuIGG L → E survey containing over 1300 PSBs, we stack spectra in bins of stellar mass, (specific) star formation rate, burst mass, burst mass fraction, and time since quenching. We observe blueshifted line centroids indicative of outflows in all stacks except the one containing galaxies that quenched more than 260 Myr ago. Outflow velocities decline with increasing time since quenching, while showing little correlation with other galaxy properties. The inferred outflows have large mass loading factors of 1–120, maximum velocities above their host-galaxy escape velocities required for gas to leave the interstellar medium, and energy and momentum fluxes exceeding those expected from the current star formation. Our results suggest that cool gas outflows are ubiquitous in intermediate-redshift PSBs and are likely relic outflows launched by previous activity from starbursts or active galactic nuclei. These outflows have the potential to quench star formation by transporting gas into the galactic halos, consistent with outflows playing an important role in rapid quenching from intermediate to high redshift.

picks.title: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
picks.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
picks.abstract: 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

picks.title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
picks.abstract: Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen-containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice-derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface-confined spillover, its atomic-scale dynamics in asymmetric multi-site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross-site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure-activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi-atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self-optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space-time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

picks.title: Fine Stratification of Survey Experiments
picks.abstract: This paper studies a two-stage model of experimentation, where the researcher first samples representative experimental participants from an eligible pool, then assigns each sampled unit to treatment or control, using matched k-tuples randomization at both stages. To implement such designs, we develop a fast algorithm for matching units into k-tuples for any k ≥ 2 and any dimension of covariates. By surveying 200 recent experimental working papers, we estimate that our algorithm newly enables multivariate fine stratification with provable match quality guarantees in about 48% of recent papers. We show that finely stratified sampling and assignment both nonparametrically reduce the variance of treatment effect estimation, with the gains from stratified sampling increasing in the size of the eligible pool and how well covariates predict treatment effect heterogeneity. We develop new inference methods that fully exploit the efficiency gains from both design stages, allowing researchers to report smaller standard errors if they designed a representative experiment. An application to nine published experiments quantifies the efficiency gains.

picks.title: Universal 3D nanoscale assembly with DNA polycubes
picks.abstract: Building three-dimensional (3D) structures at the nanoscale with control over both their shape and the placement of functional components is a central goal of nanotechnology, yet most fabrication methods remain restricted to flat or simple repetitive geometries. Self-assembly of DNA building blocks offers a route to programmable architectures, but assembling large, arbitrary 3D objects from a small and reusable set of components has remained challenging. We present here a DNA polycube platform, where cube-shaped DNA nanostructures are used as building blocks that self-assemble into larger arbitrary 3D shapes. We introduce a minimal kit design principle, where we use a multiscale simulation platform combined with constrained optimization that solves the inverse design problem by identifying the smallest number of distinct blocks that are required to assemble a target 3D shape and avoid misassembled states. We demonstrate this approach with the design and experimental realization of finite-size as well as lattice structures, including complex shapes such as a fractal Menger cube. We further introduce out-of-equilibrium rearrangement of structures, where assembled DNA polycubes can be reconfigured by introducing a set of invader cubes that displace the ones in the structure. We demonstrate the suitability of our platform for positioning different functional groups in 3D by attaching functional cargoes to the building blocks and creating a 3D carbon nanotube junction, thus opening pathways to precise 3D nanofabrication by self-assembly.

more.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
more.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

more.title: Probing the neutron skin with extreme collision geometries in heavy-ion collisions
more.abstract: Understanding how protons and neutrons are located differently in an atomic nucleus can provide fundamental information on nuclear structure and have far-reaching implications for astrophysics. A precise determination of this important difference, often quantified by the so-called neutron skin thickness, is challenging both theoretically and experimentally. Here we show a category of observables in heavy-ion collisions could directly access the neutron skin by leveraging extreme collision geometries. In super-central collisions, the neutrons in the skin have an appreciable probability of missing the bulk collisions and flying down the collision beam pipeline, thus becoming countable by dedicated detectors there. In peripheral collisions, the nucleons in the overlapping collision zone are dominantly from the neutron skin and induce a measurable isospin asymmetry. These observables are demonstrated by quantitative simulations to have robust sensitivity for constraining the thickness of both 208 Pb and 48 Ca nuclei. The asymmetric collision between 48 Ca and 40 Ca nuclei is found to be a unique and powerful way for probing the neutron skin.

more.title: Machine Learning Model for the Chemistry of a Solvated Electron
more.abstract: In molecular simulations, machine learning force fields can achieve accuracy at a lower cost but remain limited in the explicit modeling of electrons. In this Letter, we develop an electron-aware machine learning force field in which an excess electron of interest is modeled quantum mechanically, while the remaining short-range interactions and long-range Coulombic forces are machine learned to reproduce a density functional theory calculation. We demonstrate the method on the solvated electron in bulk water and its reaction with a hydronium ion. We identify a proton transfer mechanism by which the excess proton recombines with the electron. We determine the forward reaction rates between 350 and 450 K from first-passage survival functions, which yield an Arrhenius relationship with an activation energy of 3.2 kcal mol − 1, in good agreement with experiment. From an enhanced sampling simulation, we determine the equilibrium constant, and thus the reaction free energy, which is also consistent with experimental measurements.

more.title: Conservative Binary Dynamics to Third Post-Minkowskian Order beyond General Relativity
more.abstract: We present the conservative dynamics of compact binaries to third order in the post-Minkowskian approximation in a theory that extends general relativity by a massless scalar field coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant. We employ the effective field theory approach to construct the effective action of binary systems by integrating out the metric and scalar degrees of freedom that mediate the gravitational interactions between the two bodies. We derive analytical expressions for the scattering impulse and the deflection angle to third order in the post-Minkowskian expansion. Our results are found to be in agreement, in the overlapping regimes, with state-of-the-art calculations in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian theory.

more.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
more.abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

more.title: Dissipation-induced threshold on integrability footprints
more.abstract: The presence of a dissipative environment substantially disrupts unitary evolution. Nevertheless, key features of the evolution, such as its integrable or chaotic nature, are not immediately erased by dissipation. To understand this, we model environment-induced dissipation as a convex combination of unitary evolution and a random Kraus map, and examine how signatures of integrability gradually fade with increasing dissipation strength. Our analysis shows that in the weakly dissipative regime, the complex eigenvalue spectrum organizes into well-defined, high-density clusters. We estimate the critical dissipation threshold beyond which these clusters disappear, rendering the dynamics indistinguishable from chaotic evolution. This threshold depends only on the number of spectral clusters and the rank of the Kraus map. To characterize this transition, we introduce the eigenvalue angular velocity as a diagnostic of integrability loss. We illustrate our findings using several integrable quantum circuits, including the dissipative quantum Fourier transform. Our results provide a quantitative picture of how noise gradually erases the footprints of unitary integrability in open quantum systems.

more.title: Stream-driven Ignition of a Realistic Undisturbed Helium Shell on a White Dwarf
more.abstract: The dynamically driven double-degenerate double-detonation (D 6) model has emerged as a promising progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae. In this model, a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) in a close double WD binary undergoes a double-detonation triggered by dynamical mass transfer from its companion. The mass transfer stream directly impacts the surface of the primary WD, potentially igniting a helium detonation in the surface layer. The resulting shock converges in the core, triggering a carbon detonation that ultimately unbinds the star. While previous studies have demonstrated the viability of this mechanism, the conditions under which the helium shell ignites remain uncertain. We perform two-dimensional simulations using FLASH to study the feasibility of helium detonation ignition driven by stream impact on a carbon–oxygen WD with a realistic, unmixed composition profile left at the end of the previous helium-shell burning phase before the WD was formed. We model WDs with masses of 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0 M ⊙ and vary stream properties for each case. We find that stream impact leads to helium ignition in all cases, with ignition occurring at varying distances from the impact point. Ignition consistently occurs near the core–shell transition, highlighting the importance of a realistic WD profile. However, the ignition mechanism differs between models and can arise from interactions of neighboring hot, mixed regions rather than a single point. Ultimately, all but one sustain a propagating detonation capable of traversing the WD surface, which is suggestive of the D 6 model’s viability as a progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae.

more.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
more.abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) 1 , 2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus 1 , yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

more.title: Tomographer: End-to-end Redshift Distribution Estimation for Source Catalogs and Intensity Maps
more.abstract: Redshift information is central to nearly every extragalactic and cosmological application of sky surveys, yet only a small fraction of cataloged sources—and none of the photons forming diffuse backgrounds—have spectroscopic redshifts. Clustering-based redshift inference estimates the redshift distribution of an arbitrary data set through spatial cross correlation with a reference sample of known redshifts. It relies only on positional information, making it applicable to any tracer of large-scale structure, including source populations and diffuse intensity maps. Its broader adoption, however, has been limited by technical barriers: assembling and characterizing spectroscopic references, expensive pair-counting computations, theoretical corrections, and systematic control. To remove these barriers, we introduce Tomographer, an end-to-end clustering-redshift framework. The key design feature is a set of precomputed “activation maps” encoding the spatial pair information of 3 million Sloan Digital Sky Survey spectroscopic galaxies and quasars up to z ∼ 4 over 10,000 deg 2. This eliminates user-end pair counting, reducing computational scaling from O (N log N) to O (1) map multiplications. Given a source catalog or intensity map, Tomographer returns the bias-weighted redshift distribution, b (z) d N / d z (z) or b (z) d I / d z (z). We validate the framework against samples with known redshifts, demonstrate accurate uncertainty estimates, and show robustness to survey footprint, spatially varying selection functions, beam smoothing, and foreground contamination. We showcase applications to source catalogs selected by flux, color, photometric redshift, morphology, or variability, and to intensity maps from radio to X-rays. more.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
more.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

more.title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r -modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
more.abstract: The r -modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes α ≲ 1. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear l = ∣ m ∣ = 2 r -modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency f spin ≈ 792 Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small- α approximations. The star is idealized as an unmagnetized, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r -mode frequency is measured to be f r-mode = 1014 Hz for initial amplitude α 0 = 0.2. The dimensionless frequency κ ≈ 0.7197 agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. The f r-mode increases quadratically with amplitude, and κ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where α 0 is varied through the range 0.2 ≤ α 0 ≤ 1.2. The gravitational-wave strain calculated from the Newman–Penrose scalar implies h r-mode ≈ 9.7 × 10 −22 at 10 kpc for α 0 = 0.2, which agrees with Einstein’s quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g., differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

more.title: A Multimission Detection Framework for High-energy Transients: Application to a 13 yr Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT Sample
more.abstract: The detection of faint high-energy transients is becoming increasingly important in time-domain and multimessenger astronomy, particularly for identifying electromagnetic counterparts to binary neutron star mergers, high-energy neutrino events, and other weak transient phenomena. At present, the sensitivity of gamma-ray and hard X-ray searches is often limited by the detection threshold of individual instruments, leaving a population of faint transients inaccessible to single-mission analyses. To address this limitation, we develop a joint detection framework that combines trigger information from multiple detectors and assigns each candidate a joint association probability, p joint, as a function of the individual detector signal-to-noise ratios. We apply this framework to archival Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT rates data from 2013 to 2025. The method effectively separates coincident signals from accidental background associations, suppressing inconsistent coincidences while enhancing the significance of faint events observed by both instruments. We find that, under optimal conditions, a two-mission search can increase the accessible volume for short gamma-ray bursts by up to 60%. This framework provides a practical foundation for generalized multimission searches, enabling more sensitive exploration of the faint high-energy transient sky and improving the prospects for future multimessenger discoveries.

more.title: Single-Molecule DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
more.abstract: DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.

more.title: A Cu-Modified Layered Thiostannate for Selective Pb Capture from Strongly Acidic Media
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Layered metal sulfide ion exchangers are powerful platforms for soft-metal capture, but their application in strongly acidic environments requires framework stability while preserving accessible ion-exchange pathways. Here, we introduce a new series of Cu-modified SnS2-derived layered chalcogenides, AMS-8 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs), featuring labile interlayer alkali metal ions. NMS-8 (Na1.13Cu1.32Sn3.34S8·xH2O) demonstrates that Cu+ can be incorporated into the SnS2-derived AMS layered motif without disrupting the fundamental architecture. Upon acid exposure, NMS-8 undergoes Na+/H+ exchange and interlayer contraction, showing low Sn leaching in 6 M H2SO4 but substantial Sn dissolution in 6 M HCl after prolonged exposure, despite persistent powder X-ray diffraction reflections of the layered phase. NMS-8 can rapidly capture Pb2+ from water, achieving near-complete removal within 20 s under dilute conditions, a Sips-fitted capacity of 178.2 ± 12.4 mg g–1 (regression standard error), and high selectivity against common competing cations. Structural characterization supports preservation of the lamellar network and a proposed structural model featuring Cu+ displaced off-center within a distorted octahedral framework environment. In an acid mine drainage simulant, NMS-8 selectively removes Pb, Cd, and Cu under acidic multicomponent conditions while retaining its layered structure. Local structural characterization of NMS-8@Pb reveals a spatially heterogeneous Pb distribution within individual crystallites that is not appropriately described by a simple homogeneous interlayer exchange model and is consistent with local structural reorganization during Pb2+ uptake. These results highlight Cu-modified layered thiostannates as promising platforms for rapid, selective soft-metal…

more.title: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.

more.title: Subambient Synthesis of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.

more.title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
more.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
more.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

more.title: Alkali-promoted Fe-based multimetallic catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ chemicals: from reaction mechanism to catalyst development
more.abstract: hydrogenation. Several key roles of metal promoters in Fe-based catalysts are summarized and discussed, including construction of key active sites, stabilization of the active phase and regulation of the carburization process, and optimization and modulation of the active-phase electronic structure. The design and preparation of multi-metal promoted Fe-based catalysts and construction of multifunctional catalysts with zeolites are also comprehensively discussed. Ultimately, we put forward prospects for future development of high-performance Fe-based catalysts.

more.title: Advances in Synthetic Methodologies for Isotopic Labeling of Organic Molecules
more.abstract: Radioactive and stable isotopes are essential tools in the discovery and development of new agrochemical and pharmaceutical molecules. Consequently, the body of research focused on developing novel synthetic methodologies for isotope incorporation into bioactive molecules continues to grow. Progress in this field has largely been driven by innovative catalytic methods, including late-stage functionalization (LSF) methods like hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), carbon isotope exchange (CIE), molecular skeletal editing, biocatalysis, and other labeling approaches. These methods enable efficient and sustainable site-specific introduction of isotopes into bioactive molecules at late stages of synthesis. Given the broad applications across various scientific fields, this comprehensive, critical, and accessible review summarizing diverse isotope labeling methodologies will be of great benefit to researchers in academia as well as professionals in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. This review focuses primarily on recent developments in catalytic methodologies for incorporating 2H, 3H, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15N, 18O, 18F, and 34S isotopes into organic molecules, along with a brief overview of well-established methods reported in this field.

more.title: Bioorthogonal catalytic materials for precise chemical control in living systems
more.abstract: Bioorthogonal catalytic materials integrate diverse reactions, material designs, and responsive regulation for precise chemical control in living systems. Their versatility enables applications in protein engineering, diagnosis and therapy.

more.title: Effects of plastic exposure on human health
more.abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental and public health challenge, with growing evidence linking human exposure to microplastics, nanoplastics, and associated chemicals to adverse health outcomes. This review summarises current knowledge on the health effects of plastic exposure, addressing both established findings and critical knowledge gaps. We examine human exposure to plastics and associated health risks based on available clinical and epidemiological evidence. Additionally, we explore chemicals associated with plastic, including their potential as carcinogens and disruptors of endocrine and immune function. Recognising the urgent need for preventive measures, we examine emerging strategies for reducing plastic burdens, including global regulatory efforts like the United Nations Plastics Treaty and proposed public health guidelines. By integrating current evidence, this review aims to provide a foundation for advancing research and informing strategies to mitigate health risks associated with plastic.

more.title: Atlas of classical pyrochlore spin liquids
more.abstract: Frustrated magnetism in the pyrochlore lattice magnet has proven to be a most fruitful setting for the experimental and theoretical search for spin liquids. Besides the canonical case of spin ice, recent works have identified a variety of new classical and quantum spin liquids engendered by the generic nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian for that lattice. However, a general framework for the thorough and systematic classification and characterization of these exotic states of matter has been lacking, as has an list of all possible spin liquids that this model can support and, perhaps most interesting, what is the corresponding structure of their emergent field theory description. In this work, we develop such a theoretical framework to identify the interaction parameters stabilizing different classical spin liquids and derive their corresponding effective generalized Gauss’s laws at low temperatures. Combining this with Monte Carlo simulations, we systematically identify all classical spin liquids for the general nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. In doing so, we uncover new spin liquid models with exotic forms of generalized Gauss’s law and multipole conservation laws. Our approach allows us to compile an atlas of all spin liquids realized in the phase diagram, providing a global picture of their mutual connections in parameter space and transitions between them. Our work will inform future theoretical and experimental studies of classical and quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice and help rationalize the exotic properties of pyrochlore magnets.

more.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
more.abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

more.title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
more.abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

more.title: Designing fault-tolerant blind quantum computation
more.abstract: Blind quantum computing (BQC) allows a client with limited quantum capabilities to delegate quantum computations to a more powerful server while hiding the computation. Existing protocols face significant challenges when scaling to large-scale fault-tolerant computations due to large communication overhead, photon losses, and low efficiencies. We use a recently demonstrated hybrid light-matter approach [PRL 132, 150604 (2024); Science 388, 509-513 (2025)] to develop a scalable architecture for blind quantum computation. By combining high-fidelity local gates on the server’s matter qubits with delegated rotations using photons, we construct loss-tolerant blind gates that enable new algorithmic design possibilities. Using these tools, the client can compile the algorithm to meet specific privacy goals while using fewer communication resources. We then present a scalable approach for fault-tolerant blind logical algorithms that improves the error-correction threshold and increases the speed and depth of blind logical circuits. Finally, we outline how this architecture can be implemented on state-of-the-art quantum hardware, including neutral atom arrays and solid-state spin defects. These new capabilities open up opportunities for deep circuit blind quantum computing.

more.title: Coherent manipulation of interacting electron qubits on solid neon
more.abstract: Electrons trapped on solid neon surfaces serve as low-noise charge qubits with long coherence times and high operational fidelities. Such charge qubits offer full electrical control and compact device footprints, convenient for scaling up with quantum circuits. Realizing two-qubit gates on this platform is a critical step towards practical quantum information processing. In this work, we report the first experimental demonstration of coherent manipulation of multiple interacting electron-on-solid-neon (eNe) charge qubits. By exploiting the electrons naturally confined in close proximity by the surface structures of solid neon, we have achieved a direct qubit-qubit coupling strength of up to 62.5 MHz, as well as implemented cross-resonance (CR) and bSWAP two-qubit gates using global microwave drives. The natural electron confinement by solid neon mitigates the high-density-wiring challenge, simplifies the multi-qubit control, and establishes a unique path to scale up the eNe qubit platform.

more.title: Q-Zoom: Query-Aware Adaptive Perception for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
more.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
more.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) require high-resolution visual inputs for fine-grained tasks like document understanding and dense scene perception. However, current global resolution scaling paradigms indiscriminately flood the quadratic self-attention mechanism with visually redundant tokens, severely bottlenecking inference throughput while ignoring spatial sparsity and query intent. To overcome this, we propose Q-Zoom, a query-aware adaptive high-resolution perception framework that operates in an efficient coarse-to-fine manner. First, a lightweight Dynamic Gating Network adaptively bypasses high-resolution processing when coarse global features suffice. Second, for queries demanding fine-grained perception, a Self-Distilled Region Proposal Network (SD-RPN) localizes the task-relevant Region-of-Interest (RoI) directly from intermediate feature spaces. To optimize these modules efficiently, the gating network uses a consistency-aware generation strategy to derive routing labels, while the SD-RPN employs a fully self-supervised distillation paradigm. A continuous spatio-temporal alignment scheme and targeted fine-tuning then fuse the dense local RoI with the coarse global layout. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-Zoom establishes a new Pareto frontier. Using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as a primary testbed, Q-Zoom accelerates inference by 2.5× on Document & OCR benchmarks and 4.7× in High-Resolution scenarios in accuracy-matched comparisons against the baseline's peak-accuracy token budget. Furthermore, at its largest visual-token budget, Q-Zoom surpasses the baseline's peak performance by 1.1% and 8.1% on these respective benchmarks, while keeping about 0.8× of the base model's throughput at a matched token budget. These robust improvements transfer consistently…

more.title: Local Imperfect Feedback Control in Nonequilibrium Biophysical Systems Enabled by Response Constraints
more.abstract: How biological networks achieve robust control despite relying on imperfect, local information remains an important open question. Here, we identify constraints that can limit nonequilibrium steady-state responses so severely that even crude, local feedback rules can achieve globally stable control without requiring precise network design or global information. Specifically, using Markov jump processes as a framework for biophysical dynamics, we derive general nonequilibrium constraints showing that, for many classes of rate perturbations, steady-state responses have fixed signs across all perturbation strengths, so that near-equilibrium responses predict far-from-equilibrium behavior regardless of system complexity. These constraints clarify several biological phenomena: monotonicity is guaranteed whenever a perturbation acts on a single rate parameter, and nonmonotonic responses, as observed, for example, in transcription factor regulation, arise only when an input simultaneously modulates multiple rates. Even in this case, we identify a graph-theoretic concept termed “coherence” that allows for a restoration of monotonicity. We show how coherence naturally and generally emerges in classic biophysical models of adaptation, including chemotaxis and transcription factor regulation. We next show that, within a control-theoretic framework, these constraints guarantee that simple linear feedback on small subsets of kinetic rates achieves globally stable tracking and adaptation without coordinated manipulation of many regulated variables. For systems with one regulator, local stability implies global stability for arbitrary network topologies without fine-tuning. more.title: When GenAI Increases Inequality: Evidence from a University Debating Competition
more.abstract: Research on Generative AI (GenAI) and work reports both productivity-compressing and inequality-expanding effects, leaving open a central question for organizations: Who benefits from GenAI and on which specific tasks? I address this question through a randomized controlled trial in competitive university debating, where participants are randomly assigned access to GenAI. Although most previous experimental work examines the impact of GenAI on written activities and across individuals, this setting allows me to study the impact of GenAI on a knowledge-intensive spoken activity and to identify heterogeneous effects across subtasks. I find that GenAI expands performance inequality in this setting. Consistent with recent theories on GenAI and work, results show that high-ability participants experience significantly larger gains from GenAI usage than their lower-ability counterparts in judgment-intensive subtasks, whereas lower-ability individuals only improve their performance in less expert components of debating, where GenAI can be used as a substitute. If these inequality-expanding effects generalize to similar spoken settings where complex ideas must be internalized and explained, rather than simply written, they would have important implications for understanding the impact of GenAI on work and inequality. This paper was accepted by Maria Guadalupe, business strategy. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01063 .
more.topic: Labor market dynamics and wage inequality

more.title: EraseAnything++: Enabling Concept Erasure in Rectified Flow Transformers Leveraging Multi-Object Optimization
more.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
more.abstract: Removing undesired concepts from large-scale text-to-image (T2I) and text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models-while preserving overall generative quality-remains a major challenge, particularly as modern models such as Stable Diffusion v3, Flux, and OpenSora employ flow-matching and transformer-based architectures, as well as extending to long-horizon video generation. Existing concept erasure methods, designed for earlier T2I/T2V models, often fail to generalize to these paradigms. To address this, we propose EraseAnything++, a unified framework for concept erasure in both image and video diffusion models with flow-matching objectives. Central to our approach is formulating concept erasure as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem, explicitly balancing concept removal with the preservation of generative utility. To solve such problem with conflicting objectives, we introduce an efficient utility-preserving unlearning strategy based on implicit gradient surgery. Furthermore, by integrating LoRA-based parameter tuning with attention-level regularization, our method anchors erasure on key visual representations and propagates it consistently across spatial and temporal dimensions. In the video setting, we further enhance consistency through an anchor-and-propagate mechanism, which initializes erasure on reference frames and enforces it throughout subsequent transformer layers, thereby mitigating temporal drift. Extensive experiments on both image and video benchmarks demonstrate that EraseAnything++ substantially outperforms prior methods in erasure effectiveness, generative fidelity, and temporal consistency, establishing a new state of the art for concept erasure in next-generation diffusion models.

more.title: Multidimensional motor unit control after paralysing spinal cord injury using non-invasive recordings
more.abstract: Spinal cord injury results in profound motor impairment, which affects approximately 20 million people worldwide. Regaining hand use is one of their highest priorities. Interestingly, even severely affected individuals can still use spared connections to generate detectable activity (measured with electromyography) in their paralysed muscles when attempting to perform a movement. Here we asked whether participants with no hand function due to a cervical spinal cord injury could still control the activity of motor units from paralysed muscles, which we detected using high-density surface electromyographic recordings. Participants could readily control their motor units to accurately perform three different one-dimensional tracking tasks that imposed different control requirements, with performance plateauing after a few days of practice. Moreover, this accurate control readily transferred to a two-dimensional cursor navigation task, allowing participants to play a series of one-dimensional (‘Pong’) and two-dimensional (‘Snake’) games and to navigate a virtual wheelchair using three independent control signals. This robust performance was achieved despite the presence of spasticity, and even in one participant who had a motor complete injury. These findings demonstrate the promise of non-invasive motor unit recordings for restoring hand function and suggest potential avenues for rehabilitation after paralysis.

more.title: The Labor Demand and Labor Supply Channels of Monetary Policy
more.abstract: Monetary policy is typically understood to affect employment through labor demand, with the role of labor supply receiving less consideration. We estimate the response of labor market flows to high-frequency changes in interest rates around FOMC announcements and Fed Chair speeches, and find that a contractionary monetary policy shock leads to a significant increase in labor supply: workers reduce the rate at which they quit jobs to nonemployment, and non-employed individuals increase their job-seeking behavior. These effects are quantitatively important: holding supply-driven labor market flows constant, the decline in employment from a contractionary monetary policy shock would be twice as large. To interpret our findings, we estimate a heterogeneous agent model with frictional labor markets and an active extensive margin of labor supply. The model rationalizes existing estimates of modest labor supply responses to idiosyncratic transfers with our new evidence of a large labor supply response to an aggregate shock.

more.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance
more.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver-resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

more.title: Online Job Selection: Reward Rate vs. Remaining Value
more.abstract: High-throughput systems, such as cloud spot markets, adaptive large language model inference, and order consolidation in logistics, operate under capacity constraints. In these settings, decision makers must allocate fixed resources among a stream of requests with heterogeneous reward rates and service durations. A critical tension arises when capacity is saturated; the system must decide whether to continue serving an active job to harvest its remaining value or to preempt it in favor of a new arrival. This trade-off is especially subtle when a new job offers a lower immediate reward rate but a longer service duration, potentially outweighing a high-rate job near completion. To address this challenge, we introduce a general and parsimonious online allocation framework for capacity-constrained resources, where preemption is nonresumable and yields partial rewards. This abstraction captures the essential dynamics of modern resource management problems, including but not limited to those discussed earlier. We derive intuitive index-based policies and provide constant-factor competitive-ratio guarantees for their performance without requiring any forecasts of future demand. In particular, we show that two naive index-based policies have competitive ratios of 1/2 and [Formula: see text]. Our main methodological contribution is to develop a flexible framework for defining “quasiutilities” that couples the states of an online algorithm versus an offline algorithm, which reduces the design of online index-based policies to an offline geometrical problem. The framework allows us to optimize the index function, leading to an exponential-index-based policy that has an improved competitive ratio of 0.68. more.title: The influence of feedback on the baryonic content of haloes in the COLIBRE simulations
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: We present predictions for the relationship between halo gas mass fraction and halo mass, f_(gas)²⁰⁰-M₂₀₀, from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, and explore how the gas content of haloes is influenced by feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN) over time. The f_(gas)²⁰⁰-M₂₀₀ relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic, with a peak at M200 ∼ 1011.5 − 12 M⊙. Below this mass, supernova feedback efficiently expels gas from the haloes of dwarf galaxies; above it, AGN feedback efficiently depletes the haloes of galaxy groups. The relation rises for M200 ≳ 1013 M⊙, as AGN-driven expulsion becomes less efficient. The fiducial COLIBRE model yields group and cluster gas fractions that agree with Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray constraints. While these gas fractions are lower than those in simulations such as EAGLE and IllustrisTNG, they are high relative to constraints from some recent eROSITA stacking analyses, and to gas fractions in hydrodynamical and baryonification models that reproduce both the eROSITA stacks and kinetic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (kSZ) effect measurements. COLIBRE’s hybrid AGN feedback model, which combines thermal and jet-driven feedback, produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA stacks and kSZ constraints (but worse agreement with Chandra and XMM-Newton). We investigate why COLIBRE exhibits better agreement with these observational constraints in comparison to EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and explore how simulation resolution affects the impact of feedback. Our results demonstrate that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics, and can differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.

more.title: Exchange between ocean and Greenland fjords regulated by recirculating meltwater in glacial troughs
more.abstract: The Greenland Ice Sheet is rapidly losing mass due to climate warming, contributing significantly to global sea level rise and altering ocean circulation and ecosystems. Yet, the processes controlling interactions between glacial fjords and the adjacent continental shelf and slope are not fully understood, particularly the role of bathymetric troughs in modulating water exchange between the fjords and boundary current system. Here we present high-resolution shipboard, reanalysis, and numerical model data across several deep troughs in West Greenland, revealing a recurring anticyclonic recirculation of glacial meltwater within the inner Uummannaq trough, which isolates the glacial fjord from subsurface Atlantic Water inflow and thus limits oceanic heat penetration. This circulation—driven by seasonal meltwater discharge and modulated by wind forcing—contrasts with the adjacent Jakobshavn trough, where more efficient exchange prevents such retention. The presence of recirculating freshwater correlates with enhanced nutrient concentrations and isotopic signatures, suggesting broader biogeochemical impacts. Analogous recirculation patterns are also present in some East Greenland fjords where ice loss has been comparatively reduced. Our findings emphasize the critical role of fjord-shelf topography and regional dynamics in modulating Greenland’s glacial melting, freshwater export, and nutrient delivery, highlighting the need for improved representation of these processes in climate models.

more.title: Supermassive Black Holes: modelling strongly and weakly magnetised misaligned accretion disks
more.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
more.abstract: In this paper, we carry out a numerical study of spinning supermassive black holes where the angular momentum of the accretion disk is misaligned with respect to the spin vector. We conduct a parameter survey covering a range of initial disk misalignment angles (Tᵢnit=15° , 45° , 75°) with either the Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD) or Standard And Normal Evolution (SANE) magnetic field configurations, using the general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) code KHARMA. Our misaligned accretion disks are initialised around a Kerr black hole with spin a* = 0.9375. We find that models in the MAD state can align with the black hole up to ∼10 rg, even in extremely misaligned models (Tᵢnit=75^°), which has not been seen before. SANE remain misaligned up to the black hole, reaching maximum disk tilt at ∼10rg, with this radius growing as disk misalignment increases. However, the maximum disk tilt does not have a linear relationship with the initial disk misalignment, and appears to have a maximum value of ∼50○ for the black hole spin considered here. We also show misaligned disk simulations produced by KHARMA are consistent with other GRMHD codes for a variety of problems.

shortlist.title: Little Red Dots: One Photometric Tag Concealing Diverse Spectroscopic Flavors of Massive Star Formation and Black Hole Activity
shortlist.abstract: We compile JWST/NIRSpec prism and MIRI data for 249 Little Red Dots (LRDs) at 2.3 < z < 9.3, forming a representative spectroscopic subset of NIRCam-selected LRDs. We derive a median stacked spectrum covering rest-frame 0.09–1.2 μ m, with MIRI photometry extending the spectral energy distribution to 4 μ m. 49 49 Downloadable from Zenodo: doi: 10.5281/zenodo.22206191. Four additional stacks for subsamples defined by optical-to-UV luminosity ratios show that LRDs form a heterogeneous population spanning diverse continuum slopes and line properties. Assuming LRDs host supermassive black holes (BHs) surrounded by dense gas clouds, and stars accompany this core, we infer masses of M BH ∼ 10 6.0−6.5 M ⊙ and M ⋆ ∼ 10 8.3 M ⊙, corresponding to BH-to-stellar mass ratios of 1%–2%. The stacks show ubiquitous UV and optical Fe II emission, indicating a direct view of the broad-line region and high (but sub-Eddington) accretion (λ Edd = 0.6 ± 0.2). We find a significant stellar contribution in the far-UV, reaching ∼80% in the bluest systems. Possible Wolf–Rayet features (He II λ 4687, nitrogen lines) are identified, tracing a young (3–7 Myr) compact starburst event. We also detect strong Balmer breaks and atypical Balmer, Paschen, [O III], and optical and near-infrared He I line ratios, and an absorption at ∼4550 Å (probably linked to Fe II), all consistent with radiative-transfer effects in high-density gas with warm temperatures (4000–7000 K). We find a diversity of LRD flavors modulated by the luminosity ratio between a short (≲20 Myr) and intense phase of BH activity, the most extreme stage lasting ∼3–7 Myr, characterized by near-Eddington-limit radiation, and a nuclear and compact starburst dominated by massive stars (even supermassive, M SMS ∼ 10 5 M ⊙), all embedded in…

shortlist.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
shortlist.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease 1 , 2 . Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling 3 , we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

shortlist.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
shortlist.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

shortlist.title: Cycle affinity and winding localize eigenvalues of Markov generators
shortlist.abstract: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. We show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector "winding number" of some nonequilibrium cycle. In discrete and continuous unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number is determined by the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In discrete multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl–Seifert ellipse conjecture.

shortlist.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
shortlist.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

shortlist.title: Nondichroic enantio-sensitive chiroptical spectroscopy in isotropic media
shortlist.abstract: Chiroptical effects using circularly polarized light in isotropic media produce signals that change sign when switching either molecular handedness (enantio-sensitivity) or the light helicity (circular dichroism). Here, we break this enantio-sensitive-and-dichroic paradigm by measuring a new type of chiroptical signal which is enantio-sensitive but not dichroic. We photoionize chiral molecules using femtosecond laser pulses and detect the three-dimensional photoelectron momentum distribution. The non-dichroic, enantio-sensitive asymmetry is encoded in octupolar and higher multipolar terms in the photoelectron angular distribution, which appear in multiphoton or strong-field ionization with elliptically polarized fields or cross polarized two-color fields. The robustness of the enantio-sensitivity with respect to the relative phase between the vectorial components of the ionizing field represents an example of symmetry protection, and opens unexplored opportunities for imaging ultrafast dynamics in chiral molecules, such as enantio-sensitive photoelectron spectroscopy with bright squeezed vacuum states.
