shortlist.title: Probing the neutron skin with extreme collision geometries in heavy-ion collisions
shortlist.abstract: Understanding how protons and neutrons are located differently in an atomic nucleus can provide fundamental information on nuclear structure and have far-reaching implications for astrophysics. A precise determination of this important difference, often quantified by the so-called neutron skin thickness, is challenging both theoretically and experimentally. Here we show a category of observables in heavy-ion collisions could directly access the neutron skin by leveraging extreme collision geometries. In super-central collisions, the neutrons in the skin have an appreciable probability of missing the bulk collisions and flying down the collision beam pipeline, thus becoming countable by dedicated detectors there. In peripheral collisions, the nucleons in the overlapping collision zone are dominantly from the neutron skin and induce a measurable isospin asymmetry. These observables are demonstrated by quantitative simulations to have robust sensitivity for constraining the thickness of both 208 Pb and 48 Ca nuclei. The asymmetric collision between 48 Ca and 40 Ca nuclei is found to be a unique and powerful way for probing the neutron skin.

shortlist.title: Machine Learning Model for the Chemistry of a Solvated Electron
shortlist.abstract: In molecular simulations, machine learning force fields can achieve accuracy at a lower cost but remain limited in the explicit modeling of electrons. In this Letter, we develop an electron-aware machine learning force field in which an excess electron of interest is modeled quantum mechanically, while the remaining short-range interactions and long-range Coulombic forces are machine learned to reproduce a density functional theory calculation. We demonstrate the method on the solvated electron in bulk water and its reaction with a hydronium ion. We identify a proton transfer mechanism by which the excess proton recombines with the electron. We determine the forward reaction rates between 350 and 450 K from first-passage survival functions, which yield an Arrhenius relationship with an activation energy of 3.2 kcal mol − 1, in good agreement with experiment. From an enhanced sampling simulation, we determine the equilibrium constant, and thus the reaction free energy, which is also consistent with experimental measurements.

shortlist.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
shortlist.abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

shortlist.title: SQuIGG L → E: Ubiquitous Cool Gas Outflows with Large Mass-loading Factors in z ∼ 0.7 Post-starburst Galaxies
shortlist.abstract: While recent James Webb Space Telescope studies have highlighted cool gas outflows as an important mechanism for rapid quenching at z ≳ 2, such space-based spectroscopic samples remain limited in size. In this work, we search for and characterize cool gas outflows traced by Fe ii λλ 2586, 2600 and Mg ii λλ 2796, 2803 absorption in post-starburst galaxies (PSBs) at 0.5 < z < 0.9, which are accessible to ground-based spectroscopy. Utilizing the SQuIGG L → E survey containing over 1300 PSBs, we stack spectra in bins of stellar mass, (specific) star formation rate, burst mass, burst mass fraction, and time since quenching. We observe blueshifted line centroids indicative of outflows in all stacks except the one containing galaxies that quenched more than 260 Myr ago. Outflow velocities decline with increasing time since quenching, while showing little correlation with other galaxy properties. The inferred outflows have large mass loading factors of 1–120, maximum velocities above their host-galaxy escape velocities required for gas to leave the interstellar medium, and energy and momentum fluxes exceeding those expected from the current star formation. Our results suggest that cool gas outflows are ubiquitous in intermediate-redshift PSBs and are likely relic outflows launched by previous activity from starbursts or active galactic nuclei. These outflows have the potential to quench star formation by transporting gas into the galactic halos, consistent with outflows playing an important role in rapid quenching from intermediate to high redshift.

shortlist.title: Stream-driven Ignition of a Realistic Undisturbed Helium Shell on a White Dwarf
shortlist.abstract: The dynamically driven double-degenerate double-detonation (D 6) model has emerged as a promising progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae. In this model, a carbon–oxygen white dwarf (WD) in a close double WD binary undergoes a double-detonation triggered by dynamical mass transfer from its companion. The mass transfer stream directly impacts the surface of the primary WD, potentially igniting a helium detonation in the surface layer. The resulting shock converges in the core, triggering a carbon detonation that ultimately unbinds the star. While previous studies have demonstrated the viability of this mechanism, the conditions under which the helium shell ignites remain uncertain. We perform two-dimensional simulations using FLASH to study the feasibility of helium detonation ignition driven by stream impact on a carbon–oxygen WD with a realistic, unmixed composition profile left at the end of the previous helium-shell burning phase before the WD was formed. We model WDs with masses of 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0 M ⊙ and vary stream properties for each case. We find that stream impact leads to helium ignition in all cases, with ignition occurring at varying distances from the impact point. Ignition consistently occurs near the core–shell transition, highlighting the importance of a realistic WD profile. However, the ignition mechanism differs between models and can arise from interactions of neighboring hot, mixed regions rather than a single point. Ultimately, all but one sustain a propagating detonation capable of traversing the WD surface, which is suggestive of the D 6 model’s viability as a progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae.

shortlist.title: Tomographer: End-to-end Redshift Distribution Estimation for Source Catalogs and Intensity Maps
shortlist.abstract: Redshift information is central to nearly every extragalactic and cosmological application of sky surveys, yet only a small fraction of cataloged sources—and none of the photons forming diffuse backgrounds—have spectroscopic redshifts. Clustering-based redshift inference estimates the redshift distribution of an arbitrary data set through spatial cross correlation with a reference sample of known redshifts. It relies only on positional information, making it applicable to any tracer of large-scale structure, including source populations and diffuse intensity maps. Its broader adoption, however, has been limited by technical barriers: assembling and characterizing spectroscopic references, expensive pair-counting computations, theoretical corrections, and systematic control. To remove these barriers, we introduce Tomographer, an end-to-end clustering-redshift framework. The key design feature is a set of precomputed “activation maps” encoding the spatial pair information of 3 million Sloan Digital Sky Survey spectroscopic galaxies and quasars up to z ∼ 4 over 10,000 deg 2. This eliminates user-end pair counting, reducing computational scaling from O (N log N) to O (1) map multiplications. Given a source catalog or intensity map, Tomographer returns the bias-weighted redshift distribution, b (z) d N / d z (z) or b (z) d I / d z (z). We validate the framework against samples with known redshifts, demonstrate accurate uncertainty estimates, and show robustness to survey footprint, spatially varying selection functions, beam smoothing, and foreground contamination. We showcase applications to source catalogs selected by flux, color, photometric redshift, morphology, or variability, and to intensity maps from radio to X-rays. shortlist.title: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

shortlist.title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
shortlist.abstract: Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen-containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice-derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface-confined spillover, its atomic-scale dynamics in asymmetric multi-site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross-site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure-activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi-atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self-optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space-time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

shortlist.title: Fine Stratification of Survey Experiments
shortlist.abstract: This paper studies a two-stage model of experimentation, where the researcher first samples representative experimental participants from an eligible pool, then assigns each sampled unit to treatment or control, using matched k-tuples randomization at both stages. To implement such designs, we develop a fast algorithm for matching units into k-tuples for any k ≥ 2 and any dimension of covariates. By surveying 200 recent experimental working papers, we estimate that our algorithm newly enables multivariate fine stratification with provable match quality guarantees in about 48% of recent papers. We show that finely stratified sampling and assignment both nonparametrically reduce the variance of treatment effect estimation, with the gains from stratified sampling increasing in the size of the eligible pool and how well covariates predict treatment effect heterogeneity. We develop new inference methods that fully exploit the efficiency gains from both design stages, allowing researchers to report smaller standard errors if they designed a representative experiment. An application to nine published experiments quantifies the efficiency gains.

shortlist.title: Single-Molecule DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
shortlist.abstract: DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.

shortlist.title: A Cu-Modified Layered Thiostannate for Selective Pb Capture from Strongly Acidic Media
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Layered metal sulfide ion exchangers are powerful platforms for soft-metal capture, but their application in strongly acidic environments requires framework stability while preserving accessible ion-exchange pathways. Here, we introduce a new series of Cu-modified SnS2-derived layered chalcogenides, AMS-8 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs), featuring labile interlayer alkali metal ions. NMS-8 (Na1.13Cu1.32Sn3.34S8·xH2O) demonstrates that Cu+ can be incorporated into the SnS2-derived AMS layered motif without disrupting the fundamental architecture. Upon acid exposure, NMS-8 undergoes Na+/H+ exchange and interlayer contraction, showing low Sn leaching in 6 M H2SO4 but substantial Sn dissolution in 6 M HCl after prolonged exposure, despite persistent powder X-ray diffraction reflections of the layered phase. NMS-8 can rapidly capture Pb2+ from water, achieving near-complete removal within 20 s under dilute conditions, a Sips-fitted capacity of 178.2 ± 12.4 mg g–1 (regression standard error), and high selectivity against common competing cations. Structural characterization supports preservation of the lamellar network and a proposed structural model featuring Cu+ displaced off-center within a distorted octahedral framework environment. In an acid mine drainage simulant, NMS-8 selectively removes Pb, Cd, and Cu under acidic multicomponent conditions while retaining its layered structure. Local structural characterization of NMS-8@Pb reveals a spatially heterogeneous Pb distribution within individual crystallites that is not appropriately described by a simple homogeneous interlayer exchange model and is consistent with local structural reorganization during Pb2+ uptake. These results highlight Cu-modified layered thiostannates as promising platforms for rapid, selective soft-metal…

shortlist.title: Conjugation Relay Beyond Local Coordination Rebalances Oxygen Intermediate Binding at Paired Cobalt Sites
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Correlated adsorption of oxygenated intermediates at single-metal sites limits the independent regulation of elementary steps in the oxygen reduction reaction. Herein, we establish a conjugation relay that tunes a structurally conserved cobalt pair through its molecular framework and carbon interface. We construct a pyrolysis-free series comprising a dicobalt complex and two conjugated coordination polymers grown directly on Ketjen Black, progressively extending the π network while retaining comparable Co2N4O2 pockets and cobalt loadings. Microscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support comparable cobalt pairing and local coordination across the series. Comparisons with unsupported counterparts and a physical mixture help distinguish molecular conjugation, direct interfacial coupling, and conductive contact. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that molecular π extension redistributes charge around the cobalt pair and that carbon coupling amplifies this response. Within the paired pocket, *OOH spans both cobalt centers, whereas *OH remains bound primarily to one center. These distinct geometries cause their adsorption free energies to respond unequally, decreasing the ΔG*OOH – ΔG*OH offset from the 3.13 eV single-site reference to 2.62 eV for the most conjugated supported model. Potential-dependent infrared spectroscopy detects *OOH at more positive potentials as conjugation increases, supporting facilitated formation under reaction conditions. The most conjugated catalyst delivers an iR-corrected half-wave potential of 1.02 V, with only a 13 mV loss after 30,000 cycles. These findings establish conjugation beyond local coordination as a molecular design strategy for relaxing adsorption-energy correlations at multiatom catalytic sites.

shortlist.title: Subambient Synthesis of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
shortlist.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
shortlist.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.

shortlist.title: Alkali-promoted Fe-based multimetallic catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ chemicals: from reaction mechanism to catalyst development
shortlist.abstract: hydrogenation. Several key roles of metal promoters in Fe-based catalysts are summarized and discussed, including construction of key active sites, stabilization of the active phase and regulation of the carburization process, and optimization and modulation of the active-phase electronic structure. The design and preparation of multi-metal promoted Fe-based catalysts and construction of multifunctional catalysts with zeolites are also comprehensively discussed. Ultimately, we put forward prospects for future development of high-performance Fe-based catalysts.

shortlist.title: Advances in Synthetic Methodologies for Isotopic Labeling of Organic Molecules
shortlist.abstract: Radioactive and stable isotopes are essential tools in the discovery and development of new agrochemical and pharmaceutical molecules. Consequently, the body of research focused on developing novel synthetic methodologies for isotope incorporation into bioactive molecules continues to grow. Progress in this field has largely been driven by innovative catalytic methods, including late-stage functionalization (LSF) methods like hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), carbon isotope exchange (CIE), molecular skeletal editing, biocatalysis, and other labeling approaches. These methods enable efficient and sustainable site-specific introduction of isotopes into bioactive molecules at late stages of synthesis. Given the broad applications across various scientific fields, this comprehensive, critical, and accessible review summarizing diverse isotope labeling methodologies will be of great benefit to researchers in academia as well as professionals in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. This review focuses primarily on recent developments in catalytic methodologies for incorporating 2H, 3H, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15N, 18O, 18F, and 34S isotopes into organic molecules, along with a brief overview of well-established methods reported in this field.

shortlist.title: Effects of plastic exposure on human health
shortlist.abstract: Plastic pollution is a critical environmental and public health challenge, with growing evidence linking human exposure to microplastics, nanoplastics, and associated chemicals to adverse health outcomes. This review summarises current knowledge on the health effects of plastic exposure, addressing both established findings and critical knowledge gaps. We examine human exposure to plastics and associated health risks based on available clinical and epidemiological evidence. Additionally, we explore chemicals associated with plastic, including their potential as carcinogens and disruptors of endocrine and immune function. Recognising the urgent need for preventive measures, we examine emerging strategies for reducing plastic burdens, including global regulatory efforts like the United Nations Plastics Treaty and proposed public health guidelines. By integrating current evidence, this review aims to provide a foundation for advancing research and informing strategies to mitigate health risks associated with plastic.

shortlist.title: Atlas of classical pyrochlore spin liquids
shortlist.abstract: Frustrated magnetism in the pyrochlore lattice magnet has proven to be a most fruitful setting for the experimental and theoretical search for spin liquids. Besides the canonical case of spin ice, recent works have identified a variety of new classical and quantum spin liquids engendered by the generic nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian for that lattice. However, a general framework for the thorough and systematic classification and characterization of these exotic states of matter has been lacking, as has an list of all possible spin liquids that this model can support and, perhaps most interesting, what is the corresponding structure of their emergent field theory description. In this work, we develop such a theoretical framework to identify the interaction parameters stabilizing different classical spin liquids and derive their corresponding effective generalized Gauss’s laws at low temperatures. Combining this with Monte Carlo simulations, we systematically identify all classical spin liquids for the general nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. In doing so, we uncover new spin liquid models with exotic forms of generalized Gauss’s law and multipole conservation laws. Our approach allows us to compile an atlas of all spin liquids realized in the phase diagram, providing a global picture of their mutual connections in parameter space and transitions between them. Our work will inform future theoretical and experimental studies of classical and quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice and help rationalize the exotic properties of pyrochlore magnets.

shortlist.title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
shortlist.abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

shortlist.title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
shortlist.abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

shortlist.title: Designing fault-tolerant blind quantum computation
shortlist.abstract: Blind quantum computing (BQC) allows a client with limited quantum capabilities to delegate quantum computations to a more powerful server while hiding the computation. Existing protocols face significant challenges when scaling to large-scale fault-tolerant computations due to large communication overhead, photon losses, and low efficiencies. We use a recently demonstrated hybrid light-matter approach [PRL 132, 150604 (2024); Science 388, 509-513 (2025)] to develop a scalable architecture for blind quantum computation. By combining high-fidelity local gates on the server’s matter qubits with delegated rotations using photons, we construct loss-tolerant blind gates that enable new algorithmic design possibilities. Using these tools, the client can compile the algorithm to meet specific privacy goals while using fewer communication resources. We then present a scalable approach for fault-tolerant blind logical algorithms that improves the error-correction threshold and increases the speed and depth of blind logical circuits. Finally, we outline how this architecture can be implemented on state-of-the-art quantum hardware, including neutral atom arrays and solid-state spin defects. These new capabilities open up opportunities for deep circuit blind quantum computing.

shortlist.title: Coherent manipulation of interacting electron qubits on solid neon
shortlist.abstract: Electrons trapped on solid neon surfaces serve as low-noise charge qubits with long coherence times and high operational fidelities. Such charge qubits offer full electrical control and compact device footprints, convenient for scaling up with quantum circuits. Realizing two-qubit gates on this platform is a critical step towards practical quantum information processing. In this work, we report the first experimental demonstration of coherent manipulation of multiple interacting electron-on-solid-neon (eNe) charge qubits. By exploiting the electrons naturally confined in close proximity by the surface structures of solid neon, we have achieved a direct qubit-qubit coupling strength of up to 62.5 MHz, as well as implemented cross-resonance (CR) and bSWAP two-qubit gates using global microwave drives. The natural electron confinement by solid neon mitigates the high-density-wiring challenge, simplifies the multi-qubit control, and establishes a unique path to scale up the eNe qubit platform.

shortlist.title: Q-Zoom: Query-Aware Adaptive Perception for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) require high-resolution visual inputs for fine-grained tasks like document understanding and dense scene perception. However, current global resolution scaling paradigms indiscriminately flood the quadratic self-attention mechanism with visually redundant tokens, severely bottlenecking inference throughput while ignoring spatial sparsity and query intent. To overcome this, we propose Q-Zoom, a query-aware adaptive high-resolution perception framework that operates in an efficient coarse-to-fine manner. First, a lightweight Dynamic Gating Network adaptively bypasses high-resolution processing when coarse global features suffice. Second, for queries demanding fine-grained perception, a Self-Distilled Region Proposal Network (SD-RPN) localizes the task-relevant Region-of-Interest (RoI) directly from intermediate feature spaces. To optimize these modules efficiently, the gating network uses a consistency-aware generation strategy to derive routing labels, while the SD-RPN employs a fully self-supervised distillation paradigm. A continuous spatio-temporal alignment scheme and targeted fine-tuning then fuse the dense local RoI with the coarse global layout. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-Zoom establishes a new Pareto frontier. Using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as a primary testbed, Q-Zoom accelerates inference by 2.5× on Document & OCR benchmarks and 4.7× in High-Resolution scenarios in accuracy-matched comparisons against the baseline's peak-accuracy token budget. Furthermore, at its largest visual-token budget, Q-Zoom surpasses the baseline's peak performance by 1.1% and 8.1% on these respective benchmarks, while keeping about 0.8× of the base model's throughput at a matched token budget. These robust improvements transfer consistently…

shortlist.title: Local Imperfect Feedback Control in Nonequilibrium Biophysical Systems Enabled by Response Constraints
shortlist.abstract: How biological networks achieve robust control despite relying on imperfect, local information remains an important open question. Here, we identify constraints that can limit nonequilibrium steady-state responses so severely that even crude, local feedback rules can achieve globally stable control without requiring precise network design or global information. Specifically, using Markov jump processes as a framework for biophysical dynamics, we derive general nonequilibrium constraints showing that, for many classes of rate perturbations, steady-state responses have fixed signs across all perturbation strengths, so that near-equilibrium responses predict far-from-equilibrium behavior regardless of system complexity. These constraints clarify several biological phenomena: monotonicity is guaranteed whenever a perturbation acts on a single rate parameter, and nonmonotonic responses, as observed, for example, in transcription factor regulation, arise only when an input simultaneously modulates multiple rates. Even in this case, we identify a graph-theoretic concept termed “coherence” that allows for a restoration of monotonicity. We show how coherence naturally and generally emerges in classic biophysical models of adaptation, including chemotaxis and transcription factor regulation. We next show that, within a control-theoretic framework, these constraints guarantee that simple linear feedback on small subsets of kinetic rates achieves globally stable tracking and adaptation without coordinated manipulation of many regulated variables. For systems with one regulator, local stability implies global stability for arbitrary network topologies without fine-tuning. shortlist.title: When GenAI Increases Inequality: Evidence from a University Debating Competition
shortlist.abstract: Research on Generative AI (GenAI) and work reports both productivity-compressing and inequality-expanding effects, leaving open a central question for organizations: Who benefits from GenAI and on which specific tasks? I address this question through a randomized controlled trial in competitive university debating, where participants are randomly assigned access to GenAI. Although most previous experimental work examines the impact of GenAI on written activities and across individuals, this setting allows me to study the impact of GenAI on a knowledge-intensive spoken activity and to identify heterogeneous effects across subtasks. I find that GenAI expands performance inequality in this setting. Consistent with recent theories on GenAI and work, results show that high-ability participants experience significantly larger gains from GenAI usage than their lower-ability counterparts in judgment-intensive subtasks, whereas lower-ability individuals only improve their performance in less expert components of debating, where GenAI can be used as a substitute. If these inequality-expanding effects generalize to similar spoken settings where complex ideas must be internalized and explained, rather than simply written, they would have important implications for understanding the impact of GenAI on work and inequality. This paper was accepted by Maria Guadalupe, business strategy. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01063 .

shortlist.title: Universal 3D nanoscale assembly with DNA polycubes
shortlist.abstract: Building three-dimensional (3D) structures at the nanoscale with control over both their shape and the placement of functional components is a central goal of nanotechnology, yet most fabrication methods remain restricted to flat or simple repetitive geometries. Self-assembly of DNA building blocks offers a route to programmable architectures, but assembling large, arbitrary 3D objects from a small and reusable set of components has remained challenging. We present here a DNA polycube platform, where cube-shaped DNA nanostructures are used as building blocks that self-assemble into larger arbitrary 3D shapes. We introduce a minimal kit design principle, where we use a multiscale simulation platform combined with constrained optimization that solves the inverse design problem by identifying the smallest number of distinct blocks that are required to assemble a target 3D shape and avoid misassembled states. We demonstrate this approach with the design and experimental realization of finite-size as well as lattice structures, including complex shapes such as a fractal Menger cube. We further introduce out-of-equilibrium rearrangement of structures, where assembled DNA polycubes can be reconfigured by introducing a set of invader cubes that displace the ones in the structure. We demonstrate the suitability of our platform for positioning different functional groups in 3D by attaching functional cargoes to the building blocks and creating a 3D carbon nanotube junction, thus opening pathways to precise 3D nanofabrication by self-assembly.

shortlist.title: EraseAnything++: Enabling Concept Erasure in Rectified Flow Transformers Leveraging Multi-Object Optimization
shortlist.journal: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
shortlist.abstract: Removing undesired concepts from large-scale text-to-image (T2I) and text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models-while preserving overall generative quality-remains a major challenge, particularly as modern models such as Stable Diffusion v3, Flux, and OpenSora employ flow-matching and transformer-based architectures, as well as extending to long-horizon video generation. Existing concept erasure methods, designed for earlier T2I/T2V models, often fail to generalize to these paradigms. To address this, we propose EraseAnything++, a unified framework for concept erasure in both image and video diffusion models with flow-matching objectives. Central to our approach is formulating concept erasure as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem, explicitly balancing concept removal with the preservation of generative utility. To solve such problem with conflicting objectives, we introduce an efficient utility-preserving unlearning strategy based on implicit gradient surgery. Furthermore, by integrating LoRA-based parameter tuning with attention-level regularization, our method anchors erasure on key visual representations and propagates it consistently across spatial and temporal dimensions. In the video setting, we further enhance consistency through an anchor-and-propagate mechanism, which initializes erasure on reference frames and enforces it throughout subsequent transformer layers, thereby mitigating temporal drift. Extensive experiments on both image and video benchmarks demonstrate that EraseAnything++ substantially outperforms prior methods in erasure effectiveness, generative fidelity, and temporal consistency, establishing a new state of the art for concept erasure in next-generation diffusion models.

shortlist.title: Multidimensional motor unit control after paralysing spinal cord injury using non-invasive recordings
shortlist.abstract: Spinal cord injury results in profound motor impairment, which affects approximately 20 million people worldwide. Regaining hand use is one of their highest priorities. Interestingly, even severely affected individuals can still use spared connections to generate detectable activity (measured with electromyography) in their paralysed muscles when attempting to perform a movement. Here we asked whether participants with no hand function due to a cervical spinal cord injury could still control the activity of motor units from paralysed muscles, which we detected using high-density surface electromyographic recordings. Participants could readily control their motor units to accurately perform three different one-dimensional tracking tasks that imposed different control requirements, with performance plateauing after a few days of practice. Moreover, this accurate control readily transferred to a two-dimensional cursor navigation task, allowing participants to play a series of one-dimensional (‘Pong’) and two-dimensional (‘Snake’) games and to navigate a virtual wheelchair using three independent control signals. This robust performance was achieved despite the presence of spasticity, and even in one participant who had a motor complete injury. These findings demonstrate the promise of non-invasive motor unit recordings for restoring hand function and suggest potential avenues for rehabilitation after paralysis.

shortlist.title: The Labor Demand and Labor Supply Channels of Monetary Policy
shortlist.abstract: Monetary policy is typically understood to affect employment through labor demand, with the role of labor supply receiving less consideration. We estimate the response of labor market flows to high-frequency changes in interest rates around FOMC announcements and Fed Chair speeches, and find that a contractionary monetary policy shock leads to a significant increase in labor supply: workers reduce the rate at which they quit jobs to nonemployment, and non-employed individuals increase their job-seeking behavior. These effects are quantitatively important: holding supply-driven labor market flows constant, the decline in employment from a contractionary monetary policy shock would be twice as large. To interpret our findings, we estimate a heterogeneous agent model with frictional labor markets and an active extensive margin of labor supply. The model rationalizes existing estimates of modest labor supply responses to idiosyncratic transfers with our new evidence of a large labor supply response to an aggregate shock.

shortlist.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance
shortlist.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver-resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

shortlist.title: Online Job Selection: Reward Rate vs. Remaining Value
shortlist.abstract: High-throughput systems, such as cloud spot markets, adaptive large language model inference, and order consolidation in logistics, operate under capacity constraints. In these settings, decision makers must allocate fixed resources among a stream of requests with heterogeneous reward rates and service durations. A critical tension arises when capacity is saturated; the system must decide whether to continue serving an active job to harvest its remaining value or to preempt it in favor of a new arrival. This trade-off is especially subtle when a new job offers a lower immediate reward rate but a longer service duration, potentially outweighing a high-rate job near completion. To address this challenge, we introduce a general and parsimonious online allocation framework for capacity-constrained resources, where preemption is nonresumable and yields partial rewards. This abstraction captures the essential dynamics of modern resource management problems, including but not limited to those discussed earlier. We derive intuitive index-based policies and provide constant-factor competitive-ratio guarantees for their performance without requiring any forecasts of future demand. In particular, we show that two naive index-based policies have competitive ratios of 1/2 and [Formula: see text]. Our main methodological contribution is to develop a flexible framework for defining “quasiutilities” that couples the states of an online algorithm versus an offline algorithm, which reduces the design of online index-based policies to an offline geometrical problem. The framework allows us to optimize the index function, leading to an exponential-index-based policy that has an improved competitive ratio of 0.68. shortlist.title: The influence of feedback on the baryonic content of haloes in the COLIBRE simulations
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: We present predictions for the relationship between halo gas mass fraction and halo mass, f_(gas)²⁰⁰-M₂₀₀, from the COLIBRE cosmological simulations of galaxy formation, and explore how the gas content of haloes is influenced by feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei (AGN) over time. The f_(gas)²⁰⁰-M₂₀₀ relation in COLIBRE is non-monotonic, with a peak at M200 ∼ 1011.5 − 12 M⊙. Below this mass, supernova feedback efficiently expels gas from the haloes of dwarf galaxies; above it, AGN feedback efficiently depletes the haloes of galaxy groups. The relation rises for M200 ≳ 1013 M⊙, as AGN-driven expulsion becomes less efficient. The fiducial COLIBRE model yields group and cluster gas fractions that agree with Chandra and XMM-Newton X-ray constraints. While these gas fractions are lower than those in simulations such as EAGLE and IllustrisTNG, they are high relative to constraints from some recent eROSITA stacking analyses, and to gas fractions in hydrodynamical and baryonification models that reproduce both the eROSITA stacks and kinetic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (kSZ) effect measurements. COLIBRE’s hybrid AGN feedback model, which combines thermal and jet-driven feedback, produces lower gas fractions in better agreement with eROSITA stacks and kSZ constraints (but worse agreement with Chandra and XMM-Newton). We investigate why COLIBRE exhibits better agreement with these observational constraints in comparison to EAGLE and other contemporary simulations, and explore how simulation resolution affects the impact of feedback. Our results demonstrate that halo gas fractions are a sensitive probe of feedback physics, and can differ significantly between simulations that otherwise produce very similar galaxy populations.

shortlist.title: Exchange between ocean and Greenland fjords regulated by recirculating meltwater in glacial troughs
shortlist.abstract: The Greenland Ice Sheet is rapidly losing mass due to climate warming, contributing significantly to global sea level rise and altering ocean circulation and ecosystems. Yet, the processes controlling interactions between glacial fjords and the adjacent continental shelf and slope are not fully understood, particularly the role of bathymetric troughs in modulating water exchange between the fjords and boundary current system. Here we present high-resolution shipboard, reanalysis, and numerical model data across several deep troughs in West Greenland, revealing a recurring anticyclonic recirculation of glacial meltwater within the inner Uummannaq trough, which isolates the glacial fjord from subsurface Atlantic Water inflow and thus limits oceanic heat penetration. This circulation—driven by seasonal meltwater discharge and modulated by wind forcing—contrasts with the adjacent Jakobshavn trough, where more efficient exchange prevents such retention. The presence of recirculating freshwater correlates with enhanced nutrient concentrations and isotopic signatures, suggesting broader biogeochemical impacts. Analogous recirculation patterns are also present in some East Greenland fjords where ice loss has been comparatively reduced. Our findings emphasize the critical role of fjord-shelf topography and regional dynamics in modulating Greenland’s glacial melting, freshwater export, and nutrient delivery, highlighting the need for improved representation of these processes in climate models.

shortlist.title: Supermassive Black Holes: modelling strongly and weakly magnetised misaligned accretion disks
shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: In this paper, we carry out a numerical study of spinning supermassive black holes where the angular momentum of the accretion disk is misaligned with respect to the spin vector. We conduct a parameter survey covering a range of initial disk misalignment angles (Tᵢnit=15° , 45° , 75°) with either the Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD) or Standard And Normal Evolution (SANE) magnetic field configurations, using the general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) code KHARMA. Our misaligned accretion disks are initialised around a Kerr black hole with spin a* = 0.9375. We find that models in the MAD state can align with the black hole up to ∼10 rg, even in extremely misaligned models (Tᵢnit=75^°), which has not been seen before. SANE remain misaligned up to the black hole, reaching maximum disk tilt at ∼10rg, with this radius growing as disk misalignment increases. However, the maximum disk tilt does not have a linear relationship with the initial disk misalignment, and appears to have a maximum value of ∼50○ for the black hole spin considered here. We also show misaligned disk simulations produced by KHARMA are consistent with other GRMHD codes for a variety of problems.

shortlist.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
shortlist.abstract: Observations of local Seyfert galaxies show an intriguing connection between AGN luminosity and a deficit of molecular gas on ∼50 pc scales compared to 200 pc, the plausible imprint of AGN feedback. Motivated by these findings, we investigate the interplay between supermassive black hole (BH) accretion, AGN feedback, and nuclear gas reservoirs using cosmological hydrodynamic simulations implementing FIRE-3 multi-phase interstellar medium (ISM) physics and multi-component BH accretion and feedback models. Focusing on the late-time evolution of four Milky Way-mass galaxies, we find recurrent cycles of increased gas inflow toward the accretion disc, enhanced BH accretion, feedback self-regulation, and suppressed gas inflow rate until the next fuelling event. AGN winds interact with the ISM and escape preferentially through low-density polar channels after opening central cavities on ∼10–500 pc scales, regulating BH growth and producing episodic behaviour on ∼10–100 Myr timescales. The simulations reproduce the observed diversity of nuclear morphologies, gas concentrations, and AGN luminosities in late-type Seyfert galaxies, but do not exhibit a clear anti-correlation between gas concentration and AGN luminosity. Higher-luminosity AGN (LX ∼ 1041.5 − 43 erg s−1) powered by the accretion disc reservoir can coexist with feedback-driven cavities, consistent with observations, but they are more common in simulated galaxies with centrally-peaked gas distributions. Although differences in sample selection, tracer choice, spatial resolution, and stochasticity in AGN fuelling may impact underlying concentration-luminosity trends, the apparent tension between simulations and observations points to the timing between gas inflow, accretion-disc depletion, and feedback-driven clearing…

shortlist.title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint
shortlist.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b + mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

shortlist.title: Conserved T cell receptor usage underpins recognition of CD1c presenting a mycobacterial lipid
shortlist.abstract: The mechanism by which αβ T cell receptors (TCRs) recognize mycobacterial lipids presented by CD1 family members is not well understood. We used CD1c tetramers loaded with the mycobacterial phosphomycoketide (PM) or mannosyl-PM to isolate T cells from healthy blood donors and individuals from a tuberculosis (TB)-endemic region of South Africa, with higher frequencies observed in individuals from the TB-endemic region. High-throughput analysis of >200 paired CD1c-mycoketide tetramer+ αβTCRs identified a conserved TCR motif, encoded by TRBV4-1 or TRBV7-9 variable region genes in greater than half of TCRs sequenced. A cryo-EM structure of a TRBV7-9+ TCR in complex with CD1c-PM demonstrated that the TCR bound to the A'-side of CD1c, directly contacting the phospholipid antigen and F'-portal residues. Analysis of multiple T cell clones interacting with CD1c mutants suggested that this TCR docking mode is representative of the larger TRBV7-9+ T cell population. Collectively, this study provides insight into mycobacterial lipid antigen recognition by αβ T cells restricted to CD1c.

shortlist.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
shortlist.abstract: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? To answer these questions, we run a 415-village field experiment with 8,300 women living in poverty in rural Kenya. We design an 80-minute workshop to help people set higher aspirations and plan to achieve them. We cross-randomise this with large unconditional cash transfers. The workshop substantially raises aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue, and living standards 17 months later, relative to a placebo workshop. Increases in aspirations are the most likely mechanism to explain the economic effects. Cash transfers also raise aspirations, which might help to explain why transfers increase labour supply and investment. We conclude that aspirations respond to both economic and psychological interventions, contribute to investment decisions and living standards, and are important considerations for development policy.

shortlist.title: Photothermally gated nanorobots for active blood-brain barrier transcytosis and brain delivery
shortlist.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major physiological obstacle to systemic delivery of therapeutics for neurological disorders because most nanoparticles rely on passive diffusion or receptor-mediated binding that is frequently counteracted by intracellular recycling and efflux. Here, we introduce a light-activatable, self-propelled nanorobotic system, termed BrainBot, designed to actively traverse the BBB through on-demand propulsion coupled with biological targeting. BrainBots feature an asymmetric polyethylene glycol–modified (PEGylated) silica shell encapsulating a thermosensitive gas-generating fuel and a photothermal transducer, gated by a phase-change material to ensure systemic inertness. Upon near-infrared irradiation, localized photothermal heating simultaneously triggers gate melting and fuel decomposition, transforming passive nanoparticles into directionally motile nanorobots. We demonstrate that transient propulsion synergizes with surface-conjugated BBB-penetrating aptamers to enhance receptor-mediated transcytosis, yielding substantially higher BBB transport than nonpropulsive or targeting-only controls in vitro. After systemic administration in vivo, BrainBots exhibited substantially increased brain accumulation upon localized activation, without disrupting barrier integrity or inducing detectable tissue damage. In an orthotopic glioblastoma mouse model, doxorubicin-loaded BrainBots achieved enhanced brain delivery, suppressed tumor growth, and markedly reduced systemic toxicity compared with free drug administration. By converting vascular association into efficient BBB transcytosis in a defined safety window, BrainBots provide a versatile framework for noninvasive delivery of therapeutics to the central nervous system.

shortlist.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

shortlist.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
shortlist.abstract: Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. shortlist.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading. METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure–volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography). RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34–67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0–65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0–42.0] mm Hg; P <0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P <0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183–242] to 160 [IQR, 129–204] mL; P <0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6–56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2–44.4] g; P <0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P =0.002). shortlist.title: Not Learning from Others
shortlist.abstract: We study social learning using experiments where two people independently learn relevant information and can share it to make accurate private decisions. Across three experiments, people are substantially less sensitive to information others discover than to equally-relevant information they discovered themselves. This holds when they must learn information from others through discussion; when the experimenter perfectly communicates the information; and even when participants observe others’ information with their own eyes. Our results therefore stem not from a failure to elicit information from others but a systematic tendency to underweight it relative to one’s own information. Our findings illustrate a powerful barrier to social learning that might underlie many documented cases of failure to learn from others.

Interventions Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy. shortlist.title: Uncovering directionally and temporally variable genes with STAVAG
shortlist.abstract: Spatially variable genes (SVGs) are crucial for understanding spatial heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomics. Yet SVGs are challenging to align with established biological axes and lack straightforward mechanistic interpretation, thereby limiting their ability to inform downstream experiments or clinical applications. Here, we introduce the concept of directionally variable genes (DVGs) and temporally variable genes (TVGs). In addition, we propose a unified framework, STAVAG (spatial- or temporal-aided framework for identifying directionally and temporally variable g enes), that models spatial or temporal information to identify DVGs and TVGs. STAVAG effectively identifies biologically meaningful DVGs for uncovering prognostically relevant gene modules that align with the malignant–immune–stroma structure in the tumor microenvironment, identifying marker genes in three-dimensional brain data and detecting 12 polarization genes regulating planarian regeneration. Furthermore, by tracking the progression of myocardial infarction and tissue development, STAVAG reveals critical TVGs that can serve as candidate biomarkers for the ultra-acute phase of myocardial infarction. STAVAG also identifies both global and local gene modules involved in mouse placentation, as well as tissue-specific and interactive TVG modules that dynamically evolve during mouse embryonic development.

shortlist.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
shortlist.abstract: Aerial insects can effortlessly navigate dense vegetation, whereas similarly sized aerial robots typically depend on offboard sensors and computation to maintain stable flight. This disparity restricts insect-scale robots to operation in motion-capture environments, substantially limiting their applicability to tasks such as search-and-rescue operations and precision agriculture. In this work, we present a 1.29-gram aerial robot capable of hovering and tracking trajectories with solely onboard sensing and computation. The combination of a sensor suite, estimators, and a low-level controller achieved centimeter-scale positional flight accuracy. In addition, we developed a hierarchical controller in which a human operator provides high-level commands to direct the robot's motion. In a 30-second flight experiment conducted outside a motion-capture system, the robot avoided obstacles and ultimately landed on a sunflower. This level of sensing and computational autonomy represents a notable advancement for the aerial microrobotics community, opening further opportunities to explore onboard planning and power autonomy.

fundamentals.title: Fluctuation-Response Theory of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
fundamentals.abstract: A fundamental challenge in soft matter physics is to describe materials, such as the living cytoplasm and tissues, that are simultaneously active, chemically driven, and exhibit long-lasting memory of mechanical stresses. Here, we construct a generalized hydrodynamic framework at finite wave vectors and frequencies that is applicable to nonequilibrium fluids with memory. By leveraging stationary correlation identities, we derive a generalized linear response theory for nonequilibrium steady states. This framework serves as a formal extension of Onsager’s regression hypothesis beyond thermal equilibrium. Our approach provides a direct pathway to derive transport coefficients from steady-state fluctuations without the traditional Mori-Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, generalizing the Green-Kubo relations to nonequilibrium systems. As a corollary, we derive two model-free variants of the nonequilibrium fluctuation-response relation for non-Markovian dynamics. These generalized relations explicitly capture the nonequilibrium circulating currents—an out-of-equilibrium signature that is invisible to conventional scalar formulations or frameworks that treat degrees of freedom independently. Applying our theory to chemically driven active fluids reveals the emergence of active viscoelastic memory, wherein chemical reaction cycles dynamically renormalize the macroscopic viscous response. Strikingly, this active memory can induce negative storage modulus at finite frequencies, a behavior absent in ordinary viscoelastic fluids. Our first-principles framework rigorously extends linear rheology to nonequilibrium systems and provides a foundation for understanding non-Markovian dynamics across a broad range of biological and synthetic active matter.

This is a natural framework to enforce fixed magnetic moment magnitudes on the symmetry-equivalent sites as well as to exploit the spin-orbit coupling (SOC)-induced hierarchy of energy scales. When the k index is fixed to its experimental value, the number of magnetic structures generated is on average about nine, also demonstrating the high efficiency of this scheme. Next, to quantitatively assess computational and predictive performance, we perform spin density functional theory calculations for 283 materials, first carrying out self-consistent calculations for SSA structures without SOC, followed by fixed-charge calculations including SOC for the descendant oriented SSA structures. The experimental magnetic structures are reproduced as energetically most stable in 83% of cases at the SSG level without SOC and in 76% of cases at the oriented SSG level with SOC, showing that the fixed-charge scheme enables accurate evaluation of SOC-induced energy differences at low computational cost. fundamentals.title: Revealing temperature effects on sliding friction through many-body phonon dynamics
fundamentals.abstract: Despite centuries of research into friction through classical mechanics, the fundamental principles governing friction remain poorly understood, particularly its temperature-dependent nature. This study proposes a quantum theory that reexamines the fundamental principles of tribology. By employing the Feynman diagrammatic perturbation technique within the framework of quantum many-body theory, this study incorporates phonon-phonon interactions to capture the microscopic mechanisms of energy dissipation. The results demonstrate that the phonon radiation governed by harmonic interactions dominates energy dissipation at cryogenic temperatures. As temperature rises, phonon scattering governed by anharmonic interactions overtakes radiation as the primary dissipation mechanism. Further increases in temperature lead to greater damping and suppressed phonon excitation, thereby reducing energy dissipation. The competition among phonon radiation, phonon scattering, and phonon excitation gives rise to the non-monotonic temperature characteristics of friction. Notably, this non-monotonic temperature dependence is also reproduced by classical molecular dynamics simulations. This framework provides a unified understanding of disparate friction trends with temperature observed across different materials, offering insights into the fundamental mechanisms of frictional energy dissipation.

fundamentals.title: Cycle affinity and winding localize eigenvalues of Markov generators
fundamentals.abstract: The complex eigenvalues of Markov generators govern oscillatory properties of relaxation, autocorrelation, and linear response. We show that these eigenvalues are localized by nonequilibrium cycles of the generator, thus revealing a fundamental tradeoff between thermodynamic driving, oscillation, and decay of eigenmodes. Specifically, we prove that each complex eigenvalue is confined to a region determined by the cycle affinity and the eigenvector "winding number" of some nonequilibrium cycle. In discrete and continuous unicyclic systems, we also demonstrate that the winding number is determined by the ordered eigenvalue index, yielding new thermodynamic bounds on the slowest and fastest relaxation modes. In discrete multicyclic systems, our approach unifies and extends several previous inequalities and proves the Uhl–Seifert ellipse conjecture.

fundamentals.title: Atlas of classical pyrochlore spin liquids
fundamentals.abstract: Frustrated magnetism in the pyrochlore lattice magnet has proven to be a most fruitful setting for the experimental and theoretical search for spin liquids. Besides the canonical case of spin ice, recent works have identified a variety of new classical and quantum spin liquids engendered by the generic nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian for that lattice. However, a general framework for the thorough and systematic classification and characterization of these exotic states of matter has been lacking, as has an list of all possible spin liquids that this model can support and, perhaps most interesting, what is the corresponding structure of their emergent field theory description. In this work, we develop such a theoretical framework to identify the interaction parameters stabilizing different classical spin liquids and derive their corresponding effective generalized Gauss’s laws at low temperatures. Combining this with Monte Carlo simulations, we systematically identify all classical spin liquids for the general nearest-neighbor anisotropic spin Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. In doing so, we uncover new spin liquid models with exotic forms of generalized Gauss’s law and multipole conservation laws. Our approach allows us to compile an atlas of all spin liquids realized in the phase diagram, providing a global picture of their mutual connections in parameter space and transitions between them. Our work will inform future theoretical and experimental studies of classical and quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice and help rationalize the exotic properties of pyrochlore magnets.

fundamentals.title: First Principles Magnetohydrodynamical Theory for the Expanding Box Model: Effects on Expansion-induced Alfvén Wave Reflection
fundamentals.abstract: The expanding box model (EBM) has been widely employed to simulate multiscale plasma phenomena in the expanding solar wind by transforming the MHD equations to a comoving, noninertial frame. However, traditional formulations have suffered from historical ambiguity regarding the physical separation between the comoving and inertial reference frames, primarily arising from a classical approximation of an invariant magnetic field between them. To resolve this inconsistency, we reformulate the EBM from first principles using a fully covariant approach. Here, we model the expanding solar wind frame as an anisotropic expanding spacetime metric, allowing us to incorporate radial acceleration profiles and differential transverse expansion, ensuring that all physical fields are correctly transformed by expansion. We demonstrate that asymmetries identified in previous EBM-MHD literature are direct consequences of neglecting the tensorial scaling of the magnetic field. Our covariant treatment eliminates these residues, restoring symmetry in the comoving frame. Projecting our system back into the inertial frame clarifies the distinction between local plasma dynamics and plasma expansion, revealing the anisotropy of the Parker spiral as a geometric projection. Furthermore, linear wave analysis using Elsässer variables reveals that plasma expansion induces a low-frequency cutoff and geometric damping. Numerical integration demonstrates that expansion drives the reflection of Alfvén waves, generating counter-propagating modes primarily at low frequencies relative to the expansion rate, while high frequencies converge to the WKB approximation. This provides a consistent foundation for simulations, establishing that expansion can serve as a source of counter-propagating waves…
